steps.text: Combine beef and flour in a large resealable plastic bag and toss to coat evenly.
In a 6-quart saucepan, brown beef in hot vegetable oil. Season with salt and pepper, if desired.
Add diced tomatoes, beef broth, carrots, potatoes, and thyme. Bring to a boil; reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 1 hour or until beef is tender. Blend in mustard and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: French Beef Stew
raw_recipe.description: This hearty French beef stew with carrots, potatoes, and tomatoes is flavored with thyme and Dijon mustard for a rich and comforting meal.
raw_recipe.name: French Beef Stew

Add diced tomatoes, beef broth, carrots, potatoes, and thyme. Bring to a boil; reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 1 hour or until beef is tender. Blend in mustard and serve.

review.reviewBody: Great stew served with cornbread! The mustard is awesome! Here's what I did: 2 lbs beef stew meat, 3 tblsp flour, 2 tlbsp olive oil, 1 can diced tomatoes, 1 can beef broth, 1/2 cup good red wine, 4 chopped carrots, 2 stalks celery, 1/2 cup mini onions, 2 cubed potatoes, 3/4 tsp dried thyme, 1 tlbsp sugar, 1/2 tsp minced garlic, 2 bay leaves, 2 tlbsp Dijon mustard, pinch of basil, salt/pepper to taste. Thanks for sharing!

Dijon and thyme make for a unique beef stew. Changes included: added 1 T flour for extra “gravy"; 3 T olive oil; added sliced medium onion and one clove garlic; used Better Than Bouillon/ Roasted Beef Base equal to 5 cups water; cut 5 medium potatoes into 1 1/2” chunks, added last to avoid breakdown. Cooked “low+” until stewed tomato chunks broke down and flavors melded. Will make this simple yet dramatic recipe again...

This is excellent! I picked up a pound of beef stew meat for super cheap, but I wasn't sure what I was going to do with it. I found this recipe and decided to give it a go, although I had to make a few changes based on what I had on hand. I only had 1 lb of meat and tossed it with the flour and lots of black pepper. I also threw in half of an onion chopped, as I didn't have any carrots in the house. I didn't have italian diced tomatoes, so I used diced tomatoes with onion and garlic and added some italian seasoning blend. I also didn't have any beef broth, so I used water and added some beef bouillon. I simmered all of that for about an hour before adding the potatoes, as some of the reviewers said that they became mushy. About 15 minutes before it was done, I added a bag of frozen green beans. So, my total cook time was about two hours. Boy, is this good! The mustard really adds a nice, unique flavor. I am freezing this in individual portions for lunches, and I can't wait! Thanks for sharing!

This was a nice change of pace from the stew I usually make. We realy enjoyed how the dijon gave it a nice tang. The beef wasn't as tender as I normally like. To fix that problem, next time I will simmer the beef with the tomatoes and beef broth for an hour, then add the potatoes and carrots and simmer for another hour, or until the vegetables are done. I was out of thyme, so I used savory instead and it worked really well. I also threw in a chopped onion and ended up using about 3 teaspoons of dijon instead of the 2 tablespoons.

I followed the recipe fairly closely with the following changes. I browned the beef in olive oil, without flouring first. Then I drained most of the fat, using about two tablespoons to saute my mirepoix. Then I assembled the rest of the ingredients, adding enough red wine to cover, brought the stew to a boil, then finished (covered) in the oven at 350 for about two hours.

I followed recipe except I added 2 celery stalks, used 2 lbs of beef, and cooked in crockpot on high for 4 hours. This was really good and I will make again. Next time I will only use 1 tablespoon of the dijon mustard; it was just a little to overpowering.

I made this on a very snowy New England day using my crock pot because I find that slow cooking makes for much more tender beef. That being said I tried to follow the exact directions with minor changes. I first layered the beef on bottom of slow cooker (did NOT brown) sprinkling flour, salt, pepper and thyme on top. Then added sliced carrots, chopped potatoes and had to add onion wedges. Topped it with the diced tomatoes and beef broth. 8 hours on low then mixing in the Dijon mustard. It was an interesting combination and beef nice and moist. Glad that we tried it but not sure I will do it again since there are oh so many different beef stews to try!

I made some changes, but the base recipe was the same. I tossed my grass fed stew meat in gluten free all purpose flour, some garlic and pepper seasoning and some dried parsley. I browned it in cast iron pot with onion slices and some oil. Once it was brown and the bottom of the pan was nice and chunky i deglazed it with about a cup of Cabernet. Then I added a whole box of beef broth (32 oz), the 2 cans of diced tomatoes Italian style, chopped carrots, celery, and red potatoes (skin on) cubed. I also added the thyme and a splash of worcestershire sauce and let it simmer for a while. Near the end I threw in some frozen corn and frozen peas because I wanted more colors in there and of course the Dijon mustard. So many people said don't leave out the mustard so I listened and I'm glad I did. The flavor was amazing and even with all the broth I used the consistency was perfect. I tend not to measure things and just go by what I have on hand so I hope I can recreate it. Even my picky neighbor loved it. I'm only giving 4 stars because I changed it a bit. I don't know what it would be like made as is. Maybe I'll try that and update the review.

My husband and I really enjoyed this recipe. Thanks. I used 2+ pounds of beef, white yams instead of potatoes, more thyme and cooked it in a 3.5 qt slow cooker on High for 4hrs then scooped out some liquid. I put the veggies in and cooked on high for another 1.5 hrs.

Excellent recipe and easy. I just realized I forgot to add the mustard, in the end....next time. I also had to substitute chicken broth for the beef and I added some mushrooms. Very tasty and easy. I coated the beef with flour as written and browned in vegetable oil before throwing everything in the crock pot as other reviewers suggested. Then cooked about 8 hours on low. Delicious. Thanks for the recipe.

First time I've made beef stew and my family was mad that I was making it - they don't like beef stew. Turned out that they LOVED it. I did make a few changes though. I added salt and pepper to the flour, used a little more olive oil and added some butter when browning the 2 lbs of meat. Deglazed with 1/2 cup of red wine. Added celery, pearl onions and minced garlic. My family hates mustard, so I only used 1 tbs on mustard and i added it with the beef broth so cooking would mellow out the flavor. Added 1 tsb of worchester sauce, about 3 tbs of beef base and 1/2 tsp of ground celery seed. No additional salt was needed, but it did need pepper. Simmered for about 1 1/2 hours covered and 1/2 hour uncovered to thicken. Truly the BEST beef stew I've ever had.
It was just a little bland. I added a splash of red wine, which helped. I've texted a friend in france who is an excellent cook. She always has good advice. I'm awaiting her response

Not beef stew at all in my opinion. It wasn't bad but the mustard doesn't fit with the recipe and it was an odd combination with Italian style tomatoes and Thyme. I'll stick to me own beef stew thanks.
Sounds like beef stew... what makes it french? Please don't tell me the mustard.

I made this as directed. I feel like it could've used more salt, which I did add to my bowl. I also read other reviews saying it wasn't thick enough so I added a flour/water mixture to thicken it and it turned out well. Not sure I'd make it again without using some of the other suggestions, but it is an easy recipe to follow.
